DEPUTY SECRETARY OF WAR 1010 DEFENSE PENTAGON WASHINGTON, DC 20301-1010 APR - 1 2026 MEMORANDUM FOR SENIOR PENTAGON LEADERSHIP COMMANDERS OF THE COMBATANT COMMANDS DEFENSE AGENCY AND DOW FIELD ACTIVITY DIRECTORS SUBJECT: Establishing the Mission Engineering and Integration Activity The Mission Engineering and Integration Activity (MEIA) is the Department of War's new enterprise framework for delivering capability at speed to the Joint Force. The MEIA is an engineering-based system that provides Department decision-makers with the analytical rigor, technology-driven insights, and operational analysis needed to make decisions and allocate resources for the right capabilities to help solve the Joint Force's most critical operational problems. The MEIA is purpose-built to compress decision timelines, shorten development cycles, and accelerate the delivery and operational integration of technologies and capabilities that yield overwhelming combat power for the Joint Force. The MEIA Charter Memorandum designates the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering (USW(R&E)) as the Principal Staff Assistant for the MEIA. The USW(R&E), along with the Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment, will establish and chair a MEIA Executive Steering Council. The charter includes the MEIA Implementation Plan, MEIA Industry Engagement Plan and documents MEIA objectives, organizational structures, responsibilities, and key terminology. The MEIA is more than a process or organizational construct; it is the mechanism through which the Department will secure the enduring technological dominance that underpins American power. By integrating mission engineering, rapid experimentation, operational integration, and solution refinement engagements with industry into one coherent system, the MEIA ensures that technologies are designed, validated, funded, and fielded to the warfighter

Mission Engineering and Integration Activity {MEIA) Charter 1. Overview and Purpose The MEJA is institutionalized across the Department of War (Do W) pursuant to the Secretary of War memorandum "Reforming the Joint Requirements Process to Accelerate Fielding of Warfighting Capabilities," dated August 20, 2025, established under the authority of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering (USW(R&E)) and supported by the Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment (USW(A&S)). The MEJA will use the Joint Requirements Oversight Council (JROC)-prioritized joint operational problems (JOPs) to conduct mission engineering analysis, refine capability requirements, engage with industry, run iterative experimentation, and assess integration to inform operational concepts for the Joint Force. The MEJA will recommend materiel and non­ materiel solutions to address mission needs and improve outcomes for the Joint Force. The MEJA accelerates technology analysis and development to deliver capability at speed, rather than creating a new bureaucracy. This charter defines the purpose, objectives, organizational construct, roles, and responsibilities for the MEJA. It also captures the stakeholder relationships, dependencies, and interactions with the JROC and Requirements and Resourcing Alignment Board (RRAB). 2. Objectives The MEJA will provide robust analysis and experimentation, aligned to the top priority joint warfighting needs, to identify solutions that enable an integrated and effective Joint Force. The MEJA includes the following activities: a. Mission Engineering: Mission Framing and Technical Baseline Development - Execute mission engineering analytic efforts to shape and refine the problem, assess joint mission architectures, inform capability design and development requirements, and evaluate capability solutions to address the prioritized JOPs. b. FOREWORD From The Honorable Emil Michael, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering, The Honorable Michael Duffy, Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment America stands at an inflection point where the character of warfare is being rewritten by rapid technological change, accelerating threats, and competitors determined to challenge our military advantage. For decades, the Department of War relied on processes designed to reduce risk, increase oversight, and build consensus. These processes grew to meet the demands of their time, but they no longer match the pace or scale of modern conflict and restrict innovation that is choking the Department of War's ability to deliver capability. Today, our adversaries are moving faster, integrating technology more aggressively, and exploiting our bureaucratic inertia. We must embrace a new model-one that replaces prolonged deliberation with rapid delivery, replaces document-driven reviews with mission-driven engineering, and replaces incrementalism with decisive action. The Mission Engineering and Integration Activity (MEIA) represents that new model. It is how we will solve the hardest operational problems facing our Joint Force, and how we will transform innovation into war-winning capability with speed, precision, and scale. The MEIA is more than a process or organizational construct; it is the mechanism through which the Department will secure enduring technological dominance that underpins American power. The MEIA will integrate mission engineering and analysis, rapid experimentation, operational integration, and solution refinement through engagements with industry into one coherent and effective system. It will ensure needed technologies are more rapidly designed, assessed, funded, and fielded to the warfighter. The end result: unmatched military

The end result: unmatched military capability and capacity in the hands of the warfighter to deliver a decisive and credible theory of victory. This MEIA Implementation Plan marks a decisive step forward in the Department's commitment to the warfighter and the defense industrial base charged with producing the capabilities. It articulates a clear and executable approach to solving the Department's highest-priority Joint Operational Problems (JOPs). It aligns with the National Defense Strategy, the new Joint Force Requirements Process, budget modernization, and our mandate to engineer peace through strength with technological superiority. We will address critical JOPs each year through the MEIA, ensuring that the Department's most urgent challenges receive the full weight of our engineering talent, operational expertise, and resource authority. We will scale the MEIA across the enterprise, from the Office of the Secretary of War to the Military Services, the Combatant Commands, the Joint Chiefs of Staff (referred to as the Joint Staff in this Plan), and engagements with industry. Victory in the next conflict will go to the nation that adapts fastest, integrates the best, and delivers capability at speed. The MEIA is how we will ensure that our warfighters are the most technologically advanced and best equipped force on the planet and ready to win wars if needed. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY The Mission Engineering and Integration Activity (MEIA) is the Department of War's new enterprise framework for delivering capability at speed to the Joint Force. The MEIA is an engineering-based approach that provides Department decision-makers with the analytical rigor, technology-driven insights, and operational analysis needed to make decisions and allocate resources on the right capabilities to answer the Joint Force's most pressing Joint Operational Problems (JOPs). The MEIA is purpose-built to compress decision timelines, shorten development cycles, and accelerate the delivery and operational integration of technologies and capabilities that yield overwhelming combat power for the Joint Force to secure the Department's Theory of Victory in any conflict. The MEIA operates through a streamlined governance structure designed to keep decisions fast, focused, and action oriented. The Deputy Secretary of War and Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, through the Requirements and Resourcing Alignment Board (RRAB), serve as the final decision authority for resourcing and transition, and ensuring MEIA outputs translate directly into actionable Department-wide investments for the warfighter and mission success. The MEIA Executive Steering Council (ESC) provides strategic oversight and cross-enterprise alignment, directing priorities and resolving issues that span organizations. The MEIA Executive Secretariat, led by the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering, Assistant Secretary of War for Mission Capabilities and supported by the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment, synchronizes the full MEIA enterprise; manages Missions, Capabilities, and Analysis Teams (MCA Ts) and drives timelines to ensure all recommendations have the analytic rigor and operational relevance

Acquisition and Sustainment, synchronizes the full MEIA enterprise; manages Missions, Capabilities, and Analysis Teams (MCA Ts) and drives timelines to ensure all recommendations have the analytic rigor and operational relevance necessary for rapid and informed RRAB decisions. Each year, the MEIA will execute multiple cycles focused on solving Joint Requirements Oversight Council (JROC) prioritized JOPs selected by the RRAB as the Department's highest­ priority operational challenges for the Joint Force. These problems are informed by the Combatant Commands (CCMDs), grounded in Joint Staff analysis, and focused on emerging threat assessments. The MEIA fundamentally changes how the Department translates operational problems into fielded capabilities. It replaces fragmented analysis, episodic industry engagement, and disjointed technology transitions with a disciplined, repeatable system that engineers missions from the beginning, identifies and matures the best solutions with industry, validates those solutions through analysis and experimentation, and drives timely, decisive resourcing decisions through the RRAB. The MEIA framework integrates five core activities into one seamless process: 1. Mission Engineering: Defines and decomposes JOPs into mission threads, operational assumptions, and measurable outcomes and evaluates solution impact through integrated modeling, simulation, and analysis.
